title: The Bigfoot Files Have Dropped
excerpt: US Forest Service shares 3 historical reports of alleged encounters, track sightings
content:
US Forest Service shares 3 historical reports of alleged encounters, track sightings

Bigfoot just got a little more official. The US Forest Service has quietly posted three historical files on alleged sasquatch encounters in Montana and Washington, putting decades-old sightings and speculation in one government-hosted place. One file recounts Montana hunter Leo Kinney's 1940s claim that something walking on two legs carried off a whole elk, leaving only entrails and huge tracks in the snow, per Outside. Another centers on 16.5-inch footprints seen near a Plains, Montana, sawmill in 2003—prints one witness said he couldn't explain, even as he hedged on Bigfoot belief.

The most skeptical account comes from a 1982 Umatilla National Forest biologist in Washington, who concluded a set of carefully laid, four-foot-stride impressions, tied to an alleged sighting by a forest patrolman, was likely an elaborate hoax, not a 300-pound mystery creature. The Forest Service didn't say why it released the files last month. A rep says they "add to the rich tradition of folklore that surrounds our public lands," per the Washington Post. But some believers—including those inside the service—see the files as proof that something is out there, and that the government might finally be willing to discuss it.
